maya: Heads up — I reproduced a noisy perf flip on dev-sm86 with the latest runtime. With micro_batch=2 + KV cache warmup enabled, the kernel picker oscillates between flash_v3_causal and an sdpa fallback across identical requests. Latency goes from ~1.8ms to ~4.5ms depending on which kernel wins. Seen on seq_len=64, head_dim=30. Posting quick traces and repro below.

ryan: Can you paste the profiler slice and the runtime logs? Interested in the kernel probe decisions and timings. :eyes:

perf-bot: Perf trace uploaded to /artifacts/perf/1712349999/kv_flip.trace (snapshots + kernel logs) :robot_face:

liam: Minimal profiler excerpt (from the trace):
```
KERNEL_PICKER: route=causal seq_len=64 head_dim=30 micro_batch=2 kv_warmup=true
PROBE 1 -> candidate=flash_v3_causal    latency_est=1.8ms  cpu_time=0.9ms
PROBE 1 -> candidate=sdpa_v2_noncausal  latency_est=4.3ms  cpu_time=3.9ms
CHOICE -> flash_v3_causal (score=0.21)\n
PROBE 2 -> candidate=flash_v3_causal    latency_est=1.9ms
PROBE 2 -> candidate=sdpa_v2_noncausal  latency_est=4.5ms
CHOICE -> sdpa_v2_noncausal (score=0.19)  # flip
PROBE 3 -> candidate=flash_v3_causal    latency_est=1.9ms
CHOICE -> flash_v3_causal  # flips back\n```

sasha: Hmm — head_dim=30 is not a multiple of 8/16/32, so tiling and vectorization code paths differ. My intuition: the picker uses a lightweight cost model + single-probe fallback when probe_count=1 for new warm routes. KV warmup changes memory access patterns (prefetch fills KV cache) which slightly changes measured probe timings and the score ordering. With only 1 or 2 probes the decision can oscillate.

maya: Repro command I used (dev env):
```
python -m repro.run \
  --model redwood/gpt-13B-quant \
  --seq_len 64 \
  --head_dim 30 \
  --micro_batch 2 \
  --kv_warmup true \
  --profile /tmp/kv_flip.trace
```

danielle: This looks like a hysteresis/tuning problem in the kernel picker, not a correctness bug. Two proposals: 1) require N consecutive probes (N=3) before switching kernel for the same route; 2) incorporate sm_arch-aware penalty for non-warp-aligned head_dims so sdpa/flash score gap is more stable.

ryan: Agree we should avoid flapping. Any quick config we can roll to dev to validate?

sasha: I can patch runtime to set picker.probe_count=3 and picker.min_stable_duration=500ms behind a feature flag. Also add a legality check that treats head_dim%16!=0 as slightly penalized for sdpa_v2. Will add unit test that simulates repeated probes with synthetic timings.

liam: I ran a short canary with probe_count=3 on dev-sm86 + sm89 overnight. Preliminary numbers: median latency stable at ~1.9ms, flip rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2%. I'll upload more artifacts.

maya: Nice. Can you also run with micro_batch=1 and micro_batch=4 to ensure we don't regress other configs?

liam: Yup — queued. Also noticed the flip frequency correlates with KV warmup being true; when kv_warmup=false the picker is stable. So the interaction is real.

danielle: Action items: sasha to open PR with flag + unit tests (ETA: EOD tomorrow). liam to run full sweep across SM86/SM89/SM90 with micro_batch in {1,2,4} and head_dim in {28,30,32} and post artifacts (ETA: 48h). maya to add an eval to Redwood Optimize to catch head_dim nonalignment regressions in future.

maya: Thanks all — this felt noisy in prod canary today (~10% of requests hit the flipping path). Prioritize the flag behind canary. :bug: :rocket:

ryan: +1. If the PR is small we can hotpatch into dev cluster next deploy.

perf-bot: Reminder: I will create regression alert if flip_rate > 5% for 12h on prod canary route.

maya: I'll follow up with a short note in #eng-runtime when PR lands.
